text: You are fast asleep. You are not thinking about your heart, your breathing or your food. Yet all night your heart keeps beating and your stomach keeps working. So who is running the show? Let's find out.

The autonomic nervous system controls the things you do not have to think about. It runs your heart, your glands, your blood vessels, and the smooth muscles of your gut and airways. Autonomic means automatic.
It has two main teams that work in opposite ways. The sympathetic division and the parasympathetic division.
The sympathetic division is fight or flight. When you are scared or excited, your heart beats faster, your pupils widen, your airways open, and digestion slows down.
The parasympathetic division is rest and digest. It slows your heart, narrows your pupils, and wakes up your digestion. It helps your body calm down and save energy.
Think of a car. The sympathetic side is the gas pedal. The parasympathetic side is the brake. Most of the time both are working, and your body balances them second by second.

Here is a surprise. Your heart has its own pacemaker that would beat about one hundred times a minute. Yours is probably slower, because the vagus nerve is gently holding the brake. The vagus nerve carries most of the parasympathetic signals to the heart, lungs and gut.

Both divisions use a two step chain. A first neuron leaves the brain or spinal cord and reaches a cluster of nerve cells called a ganglion. A second neuron carries the message to the organ. Parasympathetic nerves release acetylcholine at the organ. Sympathetic nerves mostly release norepinephrine.

Now back to the sleeping heart. While you sleep, the brake is on. Your heart slows, your digestion works. If a loud noise wakes you, the gas pedal takes over in a second, and your heart pounds before you even know why.

This also explains a common faint. Standing for a long time, or seeing something upsetting, can make the brake pull too hard. Your heart slows, blood pressure drops, and for a moment the brain gets less blood. If you faint often, see a doctor.

Remember three things. The autonomic nervous system runs your body automatically. Sympathetic is gas, parasympathetic is brake. And the vagus nerve is the brake for your heart. Next time, the endocrine system: the slow chemical messengers of your body.
